title: Union Cabinet Gives Modi Standing Ovation, Passes Resolution Marking 25 Years in Office
excerpt: The cabinet resolution traces ten threads from Modi's Gujarat years to national policy — and came alongside approval of a Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund and a new national transport authority.
body:
• The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Narendra Modi on 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government — Gujarat chief minister from October 2001 to prime minister since 2014 — and gave him a standing ovation.
  • Briefing the media, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the milestone reflected "enduring trust": three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and three successive Lok Sabha victories, with the resolution tracing ten threads from Gujarat governance to national policy.
  • The resolution cites scale as its evidence: nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes built, and 25 crore people lifted out of poverty, alongside Gujarat-era models like SWAGAT and Jyotigram that became national programmes.
  • The same cabinet meeting also cleared a Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund and a new national transport authority; the BJP marks the milestone with a Delhi event on October 7, with traffic curbs announced on key roads.

The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government, and gave him a standing ovation — a choreographed tribute a day before he formally completes a quarter century in elected executive office.

The resolution

Modi will complete 25 years of uninterrupted service as an elected head of government on October 7 — from his swearing-in as Gujarat chief minister in October 2001 to his third term as prime minister. The cabinet resolution frames the journey as one guided by the principle of "Nation First and Citizen First," noting three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections as evidence of "the enduring trust that the public has reposed in PM Narendra Modi."

https://x.com/ANI/status/2107506987697369515

Briefing reporters after the meeting, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the feat was without parallel in recent democratic history. "People in very few countries of the world have continuously supported one leader," he said, calling it "unique" and attributing it to "his style of work, the right policies, and pure intentions."

Gujarat to India

The resolution's centrepiece is a ten-point thread connecting Modi's Gujarat years with his national leadership. It cites SWAGAT — the programme through which he personally heard citizens' grievances, which won the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010 — as the inspiration for PRAGATI, the mechanism that brings governments together to review stalled projects and accelerate completion. Similarly, Gujarat's Jyotigram scheme of separate agricultural electricity feeders became a national approach.

On welfare, the resolution connects Modi's personal history — watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels — with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare at scale: nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes built, and 25 crore people moving out of poverty.

"People in very few countries of the world have continuously supported one leader. That faith has come from his style of work, the right policies, and pure intentions."

— Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister

Beyond the tribute

The cabinet meeting was not purely ceremonial. It also approved the government's Rs 10,000 crore commitment toward an SME Growth Fund — structured as an Alternative Investment Fund to provide growth-stage equity capital to small and medium enterprises, with most of the allocation directed at manufacturing SMEs and industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities — and cleared a new national transport authority to prepare a long-term multi-modal transport master plan.

The milestone is being marked politically as well. The BJP has planned a Delhi event on October 7 to commemorate 25 years of Modi in public life, with traffic curbs announced on key roads in the capital. State cabinets have joined in: the Manipur cabinet adopted its own resolution on Tuesday expressing gratitude for Modi's 25 years of public service, citing Centre-backed development and connectivity projects in the Northeast.

Context

The 25-year milestone follows another record set earlier this year: on June 10, 2026, Modi became the longest-serving elected prime minister of India, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's 4,398 continuous days with 4,399 days of continuous service. The cabinet resolution in June had noted that India had given the NDA a third consecutive mandate — the first time in six decades — and that the prime minister was approaching 25 years as head of government.

What's next

The October 7 BJP event in Delhi will set the tone for how the party intends to use the milestone politically — expect the 25-year frame to feature heavily in the run-up to upcoming state elections and in the government's Viksit Bharat 2047 messaging. For the opposition, the question will be whether the celebration of continuity lands as a record of governance or as a reminder of unbroken incumbency.
image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Union Cabinet passed a resolution congratulating him on 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government.
nri_angle: For the diaspora, the milestone frames a leader many NRIs have watched transform from a regional figure into a global statesman; the 25-year narrative will shape how India's story is told to the world in the years ahead.
